introduction_markdown: Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour and Section II in 1 1/2 hours; you are advised to divide your time accordingly. In Section II answer EITHER a, b and c OR d, e and f of each question. For your guidance the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation of your answers. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Where necessary, assume: the acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the earth, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; the speed of light in air, $c = 3.0\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the charge on an electron, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$. Calculators are allowed.
incertitudes: Le sujet n'imprime pas de total par question : les totaux (`points` de l'exercice) sont la somme des points imprimés bloc par bloc (Section I : 6+4+8+6+9+7 = 40 ; Section II : 20 par question, soit 100 au total).

Les schémas, diagrammes et graphes demandés à l'élève (tracé de graphe, diagramme de rayons, champ électrique ou magnétique, tension d'entrée et de sortie, schéma de montage) ne sont pas produits comme figures du corrigé : ils sont décrits dans le corrigé (axes, points clés, forme).

questions.enonce_markdown: Distinguish between contact and non-contact forces. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **contact force** acts only when the two bodies are **touching** each other: for example friction, air resistance, tension in a string, the normal reaction of a surface, a push or a pull.

A **non-contact force** (field force) acts **at a distance**, with no contact between the bodies, through a field: for example the weight of a body (gravitational force), the force between two magnets (magnetic force) or between two charges (electrostatic force).

questions.enonce_markdown: Explain why an object weighs more when taken from the equator of the earth to the poles. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **mass** of the object does not change, but its **weight** is $W = mg$, so it depends on the value of $g$.

The earth is not a perfect sphere: it is flattened at the poles and bulges at the equator, so the poles are **closer to the centre of the earth**. The gravitational field strength $g$ is therefore **larger at the poles** (about $9.83\,\mathrm{N\,kg^{-1}}$) than at the equator (about $9.78\,\mathrm{N\,kg^{-1}}$). In addition, the rotation of the earth slightly reduces the apparent weight at the equator and has no effect at the poles. Since $W = mg$ with $m$ constant, **the weight is larger at the poles**.
